title: Categorize Document Production Set by Relevance and Privilege — Privilege Log and Relevance Classification Report

blind.coverage: Read task.json in full: the one-sentence instructions and all 67 criteria. Read the judge prompt and solver system prompt. Checked scoring.py, which confirms that each judge sees only the deliverables listed in a criterion's 'deliverables' field. Read these documents in full: all 9 .eml files, the Aug 28 meeting notes, the termination letter, the litigation hold notice, the benefits enrollment with its STD attachment, the Performance Concerns Summary, the demand letter and the Alderwood engagement letter. Searched or skimmed the rest: PIP (dates and 60-day terms), Alderwood draft audit (header, distribution, disclaimers), both patent documents (inventor fields, dates), env compliance memo (header, purpose), separation agreement (header and footer showing it was sent to Vasquez), board minutes (the Kirkfield M&A engagement and the GC's legal reports). Not read line by line: the invention assignment, the body of the audit findings, and the patent claims. Legal checks: read the text of Ohio Evid.R. 502 from the Ohio Supreme Court PDF. Fetched R.C. 2317.02 through WebFetch; I saw a summary with quoted language, not the raw statute. Read CourtListener snippets from Bagley v. Yale (318 F.R.D. 234) on litigation-hold privilege. I did not independently verify Ohio common-interest case law or Upjohn's adoption in Ohio; I judged those criteria reasonable without verifying them.

findings.title: Four-tier relevance labels are graded as 'the specified categories' but the instructions never specify any tiers
findings.explanation: The instructions say only 'prepare a privilege log and relevance classification report'. No document sets a review protocol. C-052 still fails any entry that does not use 'the specified categories (Highly Relevant, Relevant, Marginally Relevant, or Not Relevant)'. Nine more criteria require exactly 'Highly Relevant' (or exactly 'Not Relevant', excluding 'Marginally Relevant'). Competent reviewers commonly use other schemes: Responsive/Non-Responsive, Hot/Warm/Cold, or High/Medium/Low. A binary responsiveness call cannot produce 'Highly Relevant' at all. A four-tier scale with these exact names is a house convention, not an implicit part of a relevance report. Under all-pass scoring, choosing a different but reasonable taxonomy zeroes the run no matter how good the analysis is.

evidence.quote: Review the attached 25-document production set and prepare a privilege log and relevance classification report for all documents.
includes a relevance tier designation using the specified categories (Highly Relevant, Relevant, Marginally Relevant, or Not Relevant)
FAIL if classified at any lower relevance tier (Relevant, Marginally Relevant, or Not Relevant).

findings.suggested_fix: Put the four-tier scale, and the privilege-status labels, in the instructions. Or rewrite the tier criteria to accept the top tier of whatever scale the solver uses (e.g., 'Highly Relevant, Hot, or equivalent top-priority designation').

findings.title: C-038 requires flagging subject-matter waiver from producing a NON-privileged email; the record also shows DOC_024 is not DOC_025's parent
findings.explanation: Subject-matter waiver under Ohio Evid.R. 502(A), which applies in this Summit County case, and under FRE 502(a) is triggered only by an intentional disclosure of privileged or work-product material. Producing DOC_024, a business email between two non-lawyers, discloses nothing privileged, so it cannot waive privilege over DOC_025. A correct answer ('no waiver risk; produce DOC_024 and log DOC_025') fails C-038, which fails any answer that raises no waiver concern. The premise is also factually off. DOC_025's embedded Aug 22 Simmons email differs from DOC_024 in subject, time, opening line and figures: 7 projects, a 58% completion rate and 23% over budget, against 5 projects, a 60% on-time rate and 12% over. DOC_025's top message is from Chandrasekaran, not Bellworth. Because DOC_025 embeds the non-privileged Simmons email and Bellworth's business paragraph, 'Partially Privileged' is arguably the better call. C-037 probably tolerates that, since it fails only 'Not Privileged'.

evidence.quote: discussing the concern that producing DOC_024 alone could be argued to waive privilege on the full chain ... FAIL if the agent does not identify any subject matter waiver concern
Subject: R&D Department — Q2 Performance Metrics & Budget Review ... R&D had 5 active projects during Q2. Of those, only 3 met their scheduled milestones — a 60% on-time rate.
Subject: R&D Department — Q2 Operational Metrics & Budget Variance ... Project completion rates came in at 58% against a target of 85% ... the department ran 23% over its approved Q2 allocation
From: Priya Chandrasekaran <pchandrasekaran@meridianpolymers.com> To: Tanya Bellworth

authorities.proposition: Subject-matter waiver extends to undisclosed communications only when a disclosure of attorney-client privileged or work-product material waives the privilege, the waiver is intentional, the subjects are the same, and fairness requires considering them together.
Same subject-matter waiver limitation for disclosures of privileged material in federal proceedings.

findings.suggested_fix: Delete C-038, or rewrite it to reward correctly stating that producing non-privileged DOC_024 creates no waiver. Optionally credit noting at-issue waiver risk if Meridian later relies on counsel's view of the metrics. Fix the documents so DOC_024 is actually the parent of DOC_025, or stop describing them as one chain.

findings.title: DOC_023 must be 'Not Relevant' although it records a 2022 depression/anxiety diagnosis and plaintiff claims $500K for emotional distress and anxiety
findings.explanation: The STD attachment records a 2022 diagnosis of major depressive disorder and generalized anxiety disorder, psychiatric medications, and a 6-week leave. The demand letter seeks $500,000 for 'severe emotional distress, anxiety'. A pre-existing psychiatric condition bears directly on causation and apportionment of emotional-distress damages, which is why Ohio lifts the physician-patient privilege for communications 'related causally or historically' to mental injuries at issue once a civil action is filed. The 2022 leave also falls in the period (from mid-2022) that defense counsel wants for performance history. The company's own hold notice lists benefits enrollment records. A competent reviewer would call DOC_023 Relevant or Marginally Relevant and produce it under a confidentiality designation or protective order. C-027 fails that answer. C-026, which demands withholding or redaction, would also fail a 'produce as Confidential/AEO under a protective order' answer.

evidence.quote: Primary Diagnosis | F32.1 | Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate ... Secondary Diagnosis | F41.1 | Generalized anxiety disorder
Emotional Distress Damages: $500,000. Dr. Vasquez has suffered severe emotional distress, anxiety, reputational harm
HR records. All benefits enrollment documentation, separation agreement drafts, and internal HR memoranda pertaining to Dr. Vasquez.
FAIL if classified as Relevant, Highly Relevant, or Marginally Relevant.

authorities.proposition: When a patient files a civil action, the physician-patient privilege does not bar discovery of communications that relate causally or historically to physical or mental injuries relevant to issues in the action.

findings.suggested_fix: Accept Marginally Relevant or Relevant for DOC_023, e.g. 'PASS if the agent recognizes the medical content and either classifies it Not/Marginally Relevant or ties it to the emotional-distress damages claim'. Broaden C-026 to accept production under a protective order or confidentiality designation.

findings.title: Privilege calls and analyses are graded only inside the relevance report (and redaction guidance only inside the log) though the instructions don't route content
findings.explanation: Judges see only the deliverable listed on each criterion. Eleven criteria grade privilege status, work-product analysis or waiver analysis using only relevance-classification-report.docx. C-053 also requires a privilege label on every relevance entry. A practitioner could reasonably keep privilege determinations and analysis in the privilege log, perhaps with a 'reviewed, not withheld' section. That solver fails all of these criteria even though the analysis exists in the other file. In the other direction, C-013, C-014 and C-030 look only at the log for dual-purpose analysis and redaction guidance, which a solver might put in the report's discussion instead. The instructions ask for two documents and never say which analysis goes where.

evidence.quote: PASS if every document entry in the relevance classification report includes a privilege status designation (Privileged, Partially Privileged, or Not Privileged).
'deliverables': ['relevance-classification-report.docx']
Output: `privilege-log.docx` and `relevance-classification-report.docx`.

findings.suggested_fix: List both deliverables on the privilege and redaction criteria so the judge sees the whole work product. Or state in the instructions that the relevance report must also carry each document's privilege status and analysis.

findings.title: Litigation hold notice: the rubric fails the common practice of withholding the whole GC hold memo as privileged/work product
findings.explanation: C-028 fails a 'fully Privileged' designation, and C-030 fails any recommendation to withhold the whole document. Many courts treat counsel's litigation hold notices as privileged or work product in their entirety and order production only after a preliminary showing of spoliation. Nothing here suggests spoliation. This memo was written by the GC after suit was filed, sent only to 12 employee custodians, cc'd outside counsel, and marked privileged. Its 'preservation directive' sections are themselves legal instructions from counsel to client employees. Partial production is a defensible choice, but withholding the whole memo is at least as mainstream, and the rubric fails it.

evidence.quote: PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION ... DO NOT FORWARD OR DISTRIBUTE
FAIL if no redaction guidance is provided or if the agent recommends withholding the entire document.

authorities.citation: Bagley v. Yale Univ., 318 F.R.D. 234 (D. Conn. 2016)
authorities.proposition: Recognizes a line of decisions (e.g., McDevitt v. Verizon, E.D. Pa. 2016) holding that litigation hold notices are privileged and discoverable only after a showing of spoliation, while questioning whether that is a hard-and-fast rule.

findings.suggested_fix: Accept either Partially Privileged with redaction guidance, or fully Privileged/work product with a note that the preservation categories can be disclosed if spoliation is put at issue.

findings.title: C-018 asserts the Alderwood engagement letter 'does not reference legal counsel', but it copies the GC on reports and refers to legal counsel
findings.explanation: The engagement letter routes the draft and final Audit Reports to 'cc: Priya Chandrasekaran, General Counsel' and advises Meridian to consult its own legal counsel. The draft report is also copied to the GC. The rubric's point stands (the audit was commissioned and signed by Simmons, framed as a proactive best-practice review, and never mentions litigation). But a careful solver who accurately notes the GC copy as a factor weighing slightly toward protection may not say there is an 'absence of legal counsel involvement' and could be failed for accuracy.

evidence.quote: A copy of the draft and final Audit Reports will also be provided to the following individual: > cc: Priya Chandrasekaran, General Counsel
does not reference legal counsel or litigation ... FAIL if the agent does not mention the absence of legal counsel involvement

findings.suggested_fix: Reword: 'notes that the engagement was commissioned and signed by Simmons, was not retained or directed by counsel (the GC receives only a courtesy copy), and makes no reference to litigation'.

findings.title: Criteria use DOC_001–DOC_025 IDs that no supplied document or instruction assigns, and the numbering is not alphabetical
findings.explanation: The criteria's IDs (e.g., DOC_001 = env memo, DOC_010 = audit report, DOC_012 = meeting notes) appear nowhere in the materials the solver sees. Solvers usually number documents themselves, often alphabetically. On that ordering DOC_010 would be the meeting notes and DOC_012 the IT backup notice, which clashes with the rubric's labels. Most criteria also give the filename, which limits the damage. Still, a judge reading a solver's 'DOC_012: Not Privileged' next to a criterion about 'DOC_012 (meeting notes)' could be misled, especially on the many ID-only references (e.g., C-038, C-062).

blind.overall: The rubric is well built on the documents and targets real review issues: the PIP-to-termination gap, the metadata anomaly, the continuation-patent inventorship omission and the Simmons admissions, the dual-purpose GC notes, the pre-engagement consult with outside counsel, and common interest without a written agreement. Most document-specific privilege and relevance calls are defensible. Three defects can fail a correct answer under all-pass scoring. First, the four relevance-tier labels are graded as 'specified' although the instructions specify nothing. Second, C-038 requires a subject-matter waiver concern from producing a non-privileged email, which is wrong under Ohio Evid.R. 502(A), and it rests on two emails the record shows are not the same chain. Third, C-027 requires 'Not Relevant' for a record of pre-existing depression and anxiety despite a $500K emotional-distress and anxiety claim. Criteria that grade privilege analysis in only one deliverable, and the ban on fully withholding the litigation hold notice, add further risk to competent answers.

sol_verdicts.reason: The STD attachment records a 2022 major depressive disorder / generalized anxiety diagnosis, psychiatric medication and a 6-week leave. The demand letter seeks $500,000 for 'severe emotional distress, anxiety'. A pre-existing psychiatric condition bears on causation and damages. R.C. 2317.02(B) lifts the physician-patient privilege for conditions causally or historically related to mental injuries at issue. C-027 fails even 'Marginally Relevant'. Privacy is a reason to protect the document, not a reason to call it irrelevant.

Ohio Evid.R. 502(A), which I read in this session, and FRE 502(a) extend waiver to undisclosed material only when a disclosure of privileged material was intentional. Producing DOC_024, a business email between non-lawyers, discloses nothing privileged. The correct answer is therefore 'no waiver'. C-038 fails that answer. The record also shows DOC_025's embedded Aug 22 email differs from DOC_024 (subject, figures), so the two are not one chain.

C-052 grades 'the specified categories' (four named tiers), but the one-sentence instructions specify none, so a reasonable Responsive/Hot-Warm-Cold scheme fails. C-053, which requires privilege status in every relevance-report row, is a plausible reading of 'for all documents' but is not stated. C-059's separate CC field is a common log column, yet a combined 'Recipients' column is also standard. Those two are debatable rather than clearly wrong.

The GC wrote the hold notice after suit was filed, marked it privileged, and cc'd outside counsel. Its directives are counsel's instructions to employees. Bagley v. Yale (read in the blind pass) recognizes a line of cases treating hold notices as privileged unless spoliation is shown, and nothing here suggests spoliation. Partial production is defensible, but C-028/C-030 fail full withholding. C-029 also labels the preservation portions 'not privileged'.

On Sol's theory, no defect. The notes put 'Ops Discussion' sections (deliverables, PIP policy, restructuring) under headings separate from 'Legal Strategy', so partial privilege with redaction is the mainstream call, and C-012 is sound. C-013/C-014 remain arguable for a different reason: they read only privilege-log.docx. Dual-purpose and redaction analysis placed in the report would not be seen (see O7).

C-015 requires only that the solver identify or discuss a waiver concern, and a discussion that concludes 'no waiver because Simmons is within the Upjohn circle' satisfies it. C-016 accepts any intra-corporate privilege doctrine. Neither forces a wrong conclusion.

C-067 requires only that DOC_022 appear on the log with a common-interest basis. A provisional entry flagged as uncertain meets that and also meets C-033's 'at-risk' branch. The two criteria are compatible. Mehta faces possible re-joinder and both lawyers expressly coordinate privilege assertions, so a producing party would log the email protectively. Declining to log a counsel-to-counsel strategy email outright is not the competent default.

The inventor-list chain is among Simmons, Mehta and Park only. Aldersgate is mentioned but not included, and the content is business logistics. 'Not Privileged' is plainly correct, and the 'recognizing no attorney' clause accurately describes the record. Sol itself concluded the result is supportable.

Competent reviewers routinely use Responsive/Non-Responsive, Hot/Warm/Cold, or High/Medium/Low. A four-tier scale with these exact names is a house convention, not an implicit component of a relevance report. Under all-pass scoring, a reasonable alternative taxonomy zeroes the run however good the analysis is.

findings.title: Criteria requiring exactly 'Highly Relevant' depend on the unstated four-tier scale
findings.explanation: These criteria pass only 'Highly Relevant' and fail 'Relevant'. A solver with a three-tier scale (High/Medium/Low) probably passes, because a judge can map the top tier. A solver with a binary Responsive/Non-Responsive scheme cannot express 'Highly Relevant' at all, and a judge may fail them. Because O1 already captures the core hidden requirement, these downstream criteria misgrade only some competent answers, so I rate them arguable rather than problematic.

findings.title: Unstated schema: privilege status in every relevance-report row (C-053) and a separate CC field in every log entry (C-059)
findings.explanation: C-053 fails a relevance report that omits a privilege-status column, even when privilege is fully handled in the log. 'For all documents' can be read to call for a combined index, but the instructions never say so. C-053 also gates C-039, C-042, C-044, C-046, C-048, C-050 and C-064, which grade privilege status using only the report. C-059 requires a CC field or a 'no CC' notation in every entry. Both requirements are plausible components of the work product but are debatable as hidden requirements.

final.changes_from_blind: Sol raised no new defect-level criteria that I accept. I rejected Sol's C-012, C-015/016, C-033/C-067 and C-064 theories after checking the meeting notes, forwarded memo, joint-defense email and inventor chain. I adopted Sol's C-059 (CC field) point at arguable. I split blind O1: C-052 stays problematic, while the downstream 'Highly Relevant' criteria drop to arguable, because a judge can map a solver's top tier. I narrowed blind O2 to C-038 alone. C-037 (fails only 'Not Privileged') and C-039 are sound. I split blind O3: C-027 stays problematic, and C-026 drops to arguable in its own finding. I split blind O4 into C-053/C-059 (hidden schema) and a narrower routing finding for analysis criteria. The privilege-status criteria graded only in the report (C-039, C-042–C-050, C-064) now fold into C-053 rather than being flagged separately, since a C-053-compliant report satisfies them. I added C-029 to the hold-notice finding because it labels the preservation portions 'not privileged'. I retargeted blind O7 to the criteria that use only IDs (C-007–C-011, C-014, C-026, C-029) and dropped C-038/C-062 from it.
final.overall: The rubric is closely tied to the record and targets real review issues. Most document-specific calls are defensible: the PIP-to-termination gap, the metadata anomaly, the omission of Vasquez from the continuation patent's inventors, Simmons's admissions, the dual-purpose GC notes, and common interest without a written agreement. Sol and I independently agree on three defects that can zero out a correct answer under all-pass scoring. First, C-052 grades four relevance tiers as 'specified' although the instructions specify none. Second, C-038 demands a subject-matter waiver concern from producing a non-privileged email, which is wrong under Ohio Evid.R. 502(A), and the two emails are not in fact one chain. Third, C-027 requires 'Not Relevant' for a record of pre-existing depression and anxiety despite a $500K emotional-distress and anxiety claim. Secondary risks are arguable: hidden schema requirements (C-053, C-059), the ban on fully withholding the GC's hold notice, criteria that read only one deliverable, the overstatement in C-018/C-019, and criteria that identify documents only by unassigned DOC numbers. I found no defect in Sol's remaining arguable items (meeting-note severance, the forwarded-memo waiver discussion, the common-interest log entry, and the inventor chain).
final.coverage: In the blind pass I read all 67 criteria, the judge prompt, and the key documents in full. In this pass I read Sol's index entry and gpt-6-sol-audit.md in full. I re-read in full the joint-defense email (DOC_022), the Aug 28 meeting notes, and the inventor-list chain's headers and legal references. I also re-read the text of every criterion Sol flagged, all criteria that name relevance tiers, the deliverable fields of the privilege-analysis criteria, and every criterion that uses a DOC ID without a filename. Legal authorities: I read Ohio Evid.R. 502 and relied on R.C. 2317.02(B) and Bagley v. Yale from the blind pass (R.C. 2317.02 through a WebFetch summary with quoted language). I did not independently verify Sol's 3M Combat Arms citation, FRE 502(a) text, or Ohio common-interest case law.
